extracted.intended_audience: Law and civic education project directors with little or no grant-writing experience
extracted.subtask_short: grant writing for law and civic education
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, beginner-focused guidance on preparing competitive grant proposals for law- and civic-education projects, covering standard proposal sections, attachments, pre- and post-submission activities, and fundraising practices. Emphasizes clarity, measurability, institutional capacity, budgeting, and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction/Summary/Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: This section provides an opportunity to give a clear, concise, and well-organized overview of the proposal, using key words that the funding source has indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a strong first impression: briefly tell who you are, what needs you wish to address, what you plan to do, how you will know when you have met your goals, and exactly what you want from the funding source. Use the space on federal/state cover sheets for abstracts; letters to foundations/corporations should begin with a summary addressing these points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Needs (Stating the Problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly and concisely state the needs that the proposal is designed to address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to statistics, research, demographics, and national/state reports showing a problem exists; document that your proposed solution may be effective by summarizing research indicating promising practices. Carefully assess needs you can reasonably address with your staff and requested funding; avoid claiming you will fix long-term societal ills or vague concerns you cannot impact in a one- to two-year grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives of the Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives should describe the outcome if the agency funds your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make objectives specific and measurable. Objectives state the result of funded activities (not the activities themselves). Explicitly explain how each objective addresses needs identified in the Statement of Needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods/Activities / Plan of Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifically outline what you will do to meet each objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include who will carry out each activity, who will oversee the entire project, and the timeframe. Use timelines and organizational charts where useful. Estimate numbers of participants and specify recruitment methods, including outreach strategies for under-represented geographic/ethnic groups. Incorporate hiring plans, advisory board meetings, report/evaluation schedules, community and family involvement. If producing materials, describe approximate pages, format, production method, and distribution plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe your plan to appraise whether you have met the objectives outlined in your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how you and the agency will determine how well activities were carried out and whether they met the needs. Use evaluation during the grant to gather information for planning and improvement. Specify whether evaluations will be subjective or objective and exactly what you hope to measure. Consider requesting funds to hire an evaluation specialist to design effective tools. Be specific about the type(s) of evaluation you will provide at the end of the grant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity of the Project to Fulfill Objectives / Qualifications of Staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate why your agency and staff should be entrusted with funds and the likelihood you can carry out the activities and oversee the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide agency location and responsibilities, other supporters or cosponsors, project history and record of success, and institutional commitments/services (e.g., accounting, office space). Include brief, edited resumes or summaries of the project director's and key personnel's special qualifications and experience related to the objectives. Explain plans for sustaining the project after funding ends and whether the project can be institutionalized or continued without this funding source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget (and Budget Narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a budget narrative assuring the funder your budget is cost effective, reasonable, consistent with actual costs, and will enable project activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show matching, in-kind, or other funding sources where possible and justify every budget request in your objectives and activities section. Follow the funder's directions about what they will/will not fund and the required budget form. Example: include substitute fees borne by districts, volunteer hours, or donated duplicating services as in-kind contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and Follow Directions Precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize and submit the proposal exactly as instructed in the request for proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather required information first, then arrange it per the RFP. Failure to follow formatting, content, or attachment instructions can disqualify or lower scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Attentive to How Proposal Will Be Read and Scored
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and respond to the funder's scoring or point system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify weighted questions (some may be worth many points while others few) and prioritize clarity on high-value sections. If scoring criteria are provided, address them explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain External Review and Director Oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a knowledgeable person read and score a draft; ensure the project director reviews all drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts recommend independent reviewers before final submission. If someone else writes the proposal, the project director must still read and carefully examine all drafts — no one knows the project better than the director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Abbreviations, Jargon, and Assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Write for an external reader who may not share your office's shorthand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove internal abbreviations and acronyms (e.g., 'the department,' 'OPI,' 'LRE') and all assumptions that the reader understands your context. Use plain language so reviewers unfamiliar with your program can understand significance and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional Presentation and Mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal is a professional document representing you and your organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quality printing, proper pagination, correct spelling, and complete sentences. Appearance and attention to detail are absolute requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments: Follow Directions and Selectively Include Supportive Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide only allowed/required attachments and use them to document credibility and past success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow funder rules on attachments. Useful attachments include: list of influential/representative board members; edited resumes of key staff/consultants; map showing target areas; personal letters from credible referees with specific language about past work and importance of the project; selected agendas/newsletters/participant lists documenting success; letter from key administrator assuring agency support; brief summary of research substantiating claimed benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preproposal Development Activities (Before Submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities to undertake before writing the formal proposal to increase fit and competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact agencies to learn funding interests and eligibility (often in person). Solicit program ideas from staff, constituents, board members, teachers, students, and diverse geographic/ethnic communities. Prepare preliminary proposals/concept papers when requested (3–5 pages) that include proposal components without full detail; these may lead to invited proposals. Serve on relevant committees/task forces and invite agency key people to events so they understand your programs. Involve board/advisory members in outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award and Relationship-building Activities (After Submission/Award)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing fund development and stewardship practices after submission or award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send thank-you letters to supporters; follow reporting requirements and file timely information; publicly acknowledge funders on program materials; keep decision makers and past funders informed through newsletters and status reports; maintain contact with non-funders and solicit feedback on rejections (ask why you were not funded and how to improve). Persistence and continuous fund-raising effort contribute to future success.
